subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should protected `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` schemas remain visible to unauthorized turns when every execution path is blocked by an immutable turn policy before hooks and side effects?
rationale: This trades reduced model-visible capability disclosure for stable provider cache shape and changes the boundary from inventory filtering to execution-time authorization; code review cannot choose that security posture.

options.title: Approve execution-gated visibility
options.body: Keep stable schemas and require current-head proof that native, Codex, Copilot, CLI/MCP, queue, and recovery paths deny unauthorized execution before hooks or side effects.

options.title: Preserve inventory filtering
options.body: Reject protected-schema visibility and redesign cache stability without exposing unavailable protected tool schemas to unauthorized turns.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Land delivery and native continuation fixes separately while deferring the protected-tool policy redesign to a security-reviewed follow-up.

recommendation.title: Approve execution-gated visibility
recommendation.body: Keep stable schemas and require current-head proof that native, Codex, Copilot, CLI/MCP, queue, and recovery paths deny unauthorized execution before hooks or side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history spans the Codex routing, CLI MCP grant, and protected execution boundaries that this decision crosses.
